land.text: Egypt, with Alexandria and Barqa conferred on Ibn Tulun in summer 871

predecessors.note: Infobox predecessor 'Abbasid Caliphate'. Ahmad ibn Tulun entered Egypt on 27 August 868 and Fustat on 15 September; the Tulunids page 'regards' 873 (259 AH) as the foundation year of the emirate, which is used here (the Cliopatria row starts in 875).

land.text: Egypt and Syria, where Abbasid troops 'restored direct caliphal rule' in 905

successors.note: The infobox lists the Ikhshidid dynasty as a second successor; it took Egypt only in 935 (ikhshidid-dynasty dossier by another agent), so the Abbasids are the successor at dissolution.

capitals.name: Al-Qata'i (Fustat, Cairo)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Al-Qata'i'; Ibn Tulun left it for Syria in June 878. The Ahmad page has Ibn Tulun entering Fustat on 15 September 868; when al-Qata'i was built is not on either page.

rulers.name: Ahmad ibn Tulun
rulers.note: Infobox '868-884 (first)'; governor from 868, autonomous from 873; died at Fustat on 10 May 884.

rulers.name: Shayban ibn Ahmad ibn Tulun
rulers.note: Infobox '904-905 (last)'. Jaysh and Harun, who ruled 896-904, are named on the page without years.

keyframe_review.note: 703.6 thousand km2: Egypt and Cyrenaica (west edge 18.7E). Right for the territory but the state should start in 873 ('This year is regarded as the foundation year of the Tulunid Emirate', 259 AH), with Alexandria and Barqa 'conferred' in summer 871 and 'by 872 Ibn Tulun had assumed control of all branches of the administration in Egypt'. The infobox has no area to compare. Shape unchanged.

972.6 thousand km2: Egypt, Cyrenaica and Syria to the Euphrates (June 878: 'advanced to Homs', 'Hama, which he captured, and proceeded to Aleppo, which also fell under his control'; the Ahmad page adds Tarsus and the Cilician frontier). Right for 878-897. From 898 the Tulunids 'relinquish control over Aleppo, Qinnasrin' (treaty of 285 AH/898), which the shape keeps (see tulunids_898).

correction.text: the 878 shape without Aleppo and Qinnasrin

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 898-905: the 878 shape without Aleppo and Qinnasrin, 'compelling them to relinquish control over Aleppo, Qinnasrin, and the capitals' (treaty of 285 AH = 898 CE). The page does not say what 'the capitals' are; Cliopatria's 900-910 shape is identical to its 878 shape, so it misses this loss.

correction.text: unchanged in outline except Aleppo and Qinnasrin (see tulunids_898), ending 905 instead of 910

keyframe_review.note: 972.6 thousand km2 for 900-910, the same as 878. The page: 'In 905, the Tulunids were unable to resist an invasion by the Abbasid troops, who restored direct caliphal rule in Syria and Egypt'; the last emir Shayban ruled 904-905. The shape ends in 905 (Cliopatria's 906-910 years are Abbasid land) and loses Aleppo and Qinnasrin from 898.

ledger.note: 873: the Tulunid emirate. 'Ahmad ibn Tulun entered Egypt on 27 August 868'; 'conferred to him the authority over Alexandria and Barqa' in summer 871; 'by 872 Ibn Tulun had assumed control of all branches of the administration'; the Tulunids page: 'This year [873, 259 AH] is regarded as the foundation year of the Tulunid Emirate'. Ahmad is governor of Egypt from 868 and 'nominal autonomy' follows.

region.text: Syria from Damascus to Aleppo, with the Cilician frontier

ledger.note: June 878: Ibn Tulun takes Syria. 'in 877/8 Ibn Tulun received responsibility for the entirety of Syria and the Cilician frontier' and 'proceeded to take possession of Damascus, Homs, Hama, and Aleppo', then went on to Tarsus; the Tulunids page dates his departure from al-Qata'i to Shawwal 264 AH (June 878). Amajur governed Syria for the Abbasids until his death in 878; Ibn Tulun returned to Egypt in April 879.

Autumn 883: Tarsus is lost. The Tulunid governor of Tarsus and the Thughur died and 'his replacement, Yazaman al-Khadim, with popular backing, refused to acknowledge Tulunid rule'; 'His attempt in autumn 883 to bring Tarsus to heel failed' and the flooded camp forced 'Ibn Tulun to retreat'. The Tulunids page has Tulunid rule 'as far north as Tarsus by 890' again (re-quoted and counterpart corrected by the me-08-b reviewer).

898: Aleppo and Qinnasrin are given up. The Abbasid treaty of 285 AH (898 CE) compelled the Tulunids 'to relinquish control over Aleppo, Qinnasrin, and the capitals'; the 886 treaty had recognized their authority 'over Egypt and the regions of Syria for a thirty-year period'.

region.text: Egypt, Cyrenaica and Syria, the Tulunid lands of 898-905

ledger.note: 905: the Abbasids reconquer Egypt and Syria. 'In 905, the Tulunids were unable to resist an invasion by the Abbasid troops, who restored direct caliphal rule in Syria and Egypt.'

905: the Tulunid emirate ends with the deposition of Shayban ibn Ahmad. Infobox '904-905 (last): Shayban ibn Ahmad ibn Tulun'; the Qarmatian raids on the Levant that preceded the collapse are undated on the page.

wars.name: Tulunid conquest of Syria
wars.outcome: Ibn Tulun took Damascus, Homs, Hama and Aleppo and went on to Tarsus; Antioch resisted ('Governor Sima al-Tawil declined to submit', siege); he returned to Egypt in April 879.
wars.note: Amajur governed Syria for the Abbasids until his death in 878; his son later submitted.

wars.name: Tulunid–Abbasid conflict with al-Muwaffaq
wars.outcome: 'Open conflict between Ibn Tulun and al-Muwaffaq broke out in 875/6' but neither side moved militarily; an assembly at Damascus denounced al-Muwaffaq as a usurper in 883; the treaty of 886 recognized Tulunid authority over Egypt and Syria for thirty years at a tribute of 450,000 dinars.
wars.note: Second source: the Ahmad ibn Tulun page for 875/6 and 883.

wars.name: Abbasid treaty of 898
wars.outcome: The Tulunids gave up Aleppo, Qinnasrin and 'the capitals'.
wars.note: The page dates the treaty to 285 AH (898 CE) without describing fighting.

wars.name: Abbasid reconquest of Egypt and Syria
wars.outcome: Abbasid troops 'restored direct caliphal rule in Syria and Egypt' in 905 after the Qarmatians swept through the Levant.
wars.note: The Qarmatian raids on the Levant that preceded it are undated on the page, so only 905 is given.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary; Egypt's Nile valley is firm, the Cyrenaican edge towards Ifriqiya and the Syrian-Jazira edge towards the Euphrates are approximate. The 886 and 898 treaties give no lines.

sources.title: Tulunids
sources.note: Identity, 873 foundation, Syria 878, treaties of 886 and 898, 905 reconquest.

sources.title: Ahmad ibn Tulun
sources.note: Entry into Egypt 868, Alexandria and Barqa 871, Syria 877/8, Tarsus 883, death 884.

notes: Cliopatria's Tulunid row runs 875..910; the dossier runs 873..905 (foundation year per the Tulunids page; Abbasid reconquest 905) and adds a 898 keyframe for the loss of Aleppo and Qinnasrin that the 900 shape (identical in area to 878) lacks. Neither page gives an area, so no infobox comparison could be made. Unsettled: the 'capitals' relinquished in 898 (probably the border cities of the Cilician frontier, not on the page); who took Tarsus in 883; the Qarmatian invasion year; the Tulunid-Makuria and Tulunid-Aghlabid borders (Cliopatria lists both as neighbours 875-910; neither page mentions Makuria and the Ahmad page says only 'to a lesser extent the eastern parts of the Maghreb' and a defeat of Abbas by the Ifriqiyans in the winter of 880-881). The Tulunid vassal status ('the dynasty's status as vassals to the caliphate', tribute of 450,000 dinars a year) is recorded by the Abbasid dossier, not here. Counterpart dossiers: abbasid-caliphate (me-08, another part), ikhshidid-dynasty (exists), emirate-of-tarsus (exists, not used), qarmatians (exists).
